speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing this severe itching and fatigue, and have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, have you experienced any recent gastrointestinal bleeding or changes in your bowel habits? I also need to know if you have noticed any jaundice or right upper quadrant abdominal pain.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you consume alcohol regularly, and have you taken any new medications or herbal supplements recently? I also need to know if you have experienced any recent fever or unintended weight loss.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Hepatitis_B_Serology, Hepatitis_C_Serology, Autoimmune_Liver_Panels (AMA, ANA, SMA).

Given your ulcerative colitis and sexual history, I need to rule out Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis and viral hepatitis, so I am ordering these blood tests immediately.

Do you have any other symptoms like night sweats or a history of gallstones?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 37.3°C (99.1°F), Blood Pressure 130/84 mmHg, Heart Rate 86 bpm, Respiratory Rate Normal. General Appearance: No acute distress. Skin: Scleral icterus and multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities. Abdominal Exam: Soft, non-tender, no distension, normal bowel sounds, no hepatosplenomegaly. Blood Work: Hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, Leukocyte Count 7500/mm3, Platelet Count 280,000/mm3, Na 138 mEq/L, K 4.7 mEq/L, Total Bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT

speaker: Doctor
text: I see your Alkaline Phosphatase is significantly elevated with only mild transaminitis, which strongly suggests a cholestatic process. Since we are investigating Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis given your ulcerative colitis history, I need to visualize your bile ducts. REQUEST TEST: MRCP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Findings show thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation. Blood Work: Alkaline Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L, Total Bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, Anti-Nuclear Antibody Negative, Antimitochondrial Antibodies Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound showing bile duct thickening and dilatation, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis and cholestatic lab results, strongly points to a specific diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
